newsitem.title: POLAND: PPABANK TO OFFER RIGHTS SHARES TO FUND.
newsitem.headline: PPABANK TO OFFER RIGHTS SHARES TO FUND.

text.p: One of the owners of Polish bank Pierwszy Polsko-Amerykanski Bank SA (PPABank) will waive its preemptive rights at the bank's upcoming issue to allow a U.S. investment fund to buy shares, PPABank said.
The bank's one-for-four rights issue of up to 1.25 million shares at 15.5 zlotys each started on Monday.

"(PPABank's) board believes that present shareholders are most important, but...one American off-shore fund is interested in aquiring shares of our new issue," PPABank deputy president Benjamin Turnbull told a news conference late on Wednesday.

Turnbull said that either the Enterprise Credit Corporation, which has a 29.3-percent stake in PPABank, or the Polish-American Enterprise Fund, with a 25.4-percent stake, would waive their rights at the issue, enabling the unnamed off-shore U.S. fund to buy at least 250,000 shares.
A first subscription period lasts until February 3 and a second phase from February 24 to March 10 will be carried out if the first period is not fully subscribed. The record date is Janurary 6.
The bank currently has five million shares outstanding.
